title: R' Avin (Ravin) bar Rav Adda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman states that he and his brother Rava were students of Rav Yehuda. Hyman continues: In Beitzah33b they said, “When we were at Rav Yehuda’s house, he would split and give to us”; and in Taanit24b and Ketubot40b, both of them spoke in the name of Rav Yehuda; and in Yoma53b they said it in the name of Rav, but Hyman says it should read “in the name of Rav Yehuda,” as in the reading of Dikdukei Soferim; and in Kiddushin70b: “R' Avin bar Rav Ada said: Rav”; and the reading of the Yalkut on Psalms, section122, is: “Rava said, Rav Ada said, Rav said.”

So too we find in Berakhot6a and Pesachim8b: “R' Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of R' Yitzchak”; Hyman says it should read likewise in Pesachim34a, where he identifies “Rabbi Avin bar Rav Acha” as the mistaken reading. So too we find in Eruvin8a, 11a and99b, and Bava Metzia116b, that he spoke in the name of R' Yitzchak; Hyman says it should read likewise in Kiddushin25a (the supplied text also adds כב,22) and Niddah66b.

Hyman further cites Niddah27a: “R' Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of Rav Menachem, a man of Kfar Shearim”; and in Yoma3a: he said to Rava (Hyman says it should read: to Rabbah), “Your students—Rav Amram and all the great ones of the generation—say,” etc.
Hyman concludes: “From all this we see that he was a student of Rav Yehuda and a colleague of Rabbah.”
